exposure: Mode of delivery (Cesarean section vs. vaginal birth)
cohort: 888 very low birth weight (VLBW) infants (≤1,500 g)
finding: Delayed cord clamping (DCC) for 45 seconds was associated with increased hemoglobin levels at birth and close to discharge, and reduced the need for blood transfusion in VLBW infants.
mod_finding: DCC for 45 seconds was equally effective for infants born by Cesarean section and vaginal delivery.
